add.issue.name: Detect a conflicted or unparseable .epiq/project.json and warn the user

edit.description.md:
Connecting a repo edits `.epiq/project.json`, which users commit on their own branches. Two branches that both connect a repo conflict on its `repos` array. While the file holds conflict markers or invalid JSON, epiq fails to read `projectId`/`stateBranch` (git-constants.ts: "Unable to read project.json"), so the whole board likely stops working, not just the repo list.

Wanted: detect it (conflict markers specifically, otherwise invalid JSON) and tell the user in the GUI, TUI and MCP which file is broken and how to fix it (resolve the conflict, keep both entries), instead of failing with a generic error.

Moot if the repo list moves off project.json; see the question raised under JG726MS.

The feature is unreleased, so the project.json form can be dropped. Plan to be agreed with claude/reviewer before implementing. Also check epiq's own project.json is intact.

Supersedes 71QKQRP if nothing edits project.json after init.

add.issue.name: Connected repos refuse local file:/// paths: only what every contributor can fetch

edit.description.md: jola: a connected repo must be something every contributor can fetch and agree on over the network. A file:/// path names one machine (and leaks a home directory into the permanent log), so it is refused when connecting and never listed by readers. The fold keeps such events, so builds agree on the log. EPIQ_ALLOW_LOCAL_REPOS=1 allows them for epiq's own test suites.

add.issue.name: GUI: a page and a server from different epiq builds must not talk; reload or say so

edit.description.md:
Hit by jola on 2026-10-14: a newer page reconnected to an older server and got "Invalid message: type: Invalid discriminator value" for repos:get. A user hits the same after upgrading or downgrading epiq while a tab stays open (its websocket reconnects without reloading), or with two epiq versions on one machine.

Wanted:
1. On every (re)connect the server says which build it is; a page from another build reloads itself instead of sending messages the server cannot read.
2. `epiq gui` reuses a running server for the same repo without checking its version (gui/init.ts probeGuiInstance). A different version should be replaced or named, not silently reused.

The version string alone misses dev builds (every build says 1.12.4 until a release), so compare a build id as well.

add.issue.name: TUI heap grows until OOM: released builds run React's development build (GH #470)

edit.description.md:
GH #470: two users' TUIs die at ~4 GB heap after 12-19 h.

Cause: neither the SEA binary nor the npm bin sets NODE_ENV=production, so React and react-reconciler load their development builds. Those log a `performance.measure` per render commit (with a props diff), and Node keeps every measure for the life of the process.

Repro: TUI + a second writer on the same worktree (as with a GUI server beside it). Released 1.13.0 binary: post-GC heap 29 → 76 MB in 2 min, 46k PerformanceMeasure objects retained. Fixed builds: flat at ~25-28 MB.

Fix:
- build-sea.mjs: `--define:process.env.NODE_ENV="production"`
- npm: new `source/cli.ts` launcher sets `NODE_ENV ??= 'production'` then dynamically imports the app; built with `--splitting` so the externals load after it
- e2e test: the npm bin loads no `.development.` React file

edit.description.md:
GH #470: two users' TUIs die at ~4 GB heap after 12-19 h.

Cause: neither the SEA binary nor the npm bins set NODE_ENV=production, so React and react-reconciler load their development builds. Those log a `performance.measure` per render commit (with a props diff), and Node keeps every measure for the life of the process.

Repro: TUI + a second writer on the same worktree (as with a GUI server beside it). Released 1.13.0 binary: post-GC heap 29 → 76 MB in 2 min, 46k PerformanceMeasure objects retained. Fixed builds: flat at ~25-28 MB.

Fix:
- build-sea.mjs: `--define:process.env.NODE_ENV="production"`
- npm `epiq`: new `source/cli.ts` launcher sets `NODE_ENV ||= 'production'` then dynamically imports the app
